metadata.subject: Computer Networks
metadata.title: Choose TCP or UDP
metadata.description: Predict and inspect how TCP-like and UDP transport react to delay, loss, and reordered arrival.

learning_objectives: Distinguish network loss from protocol behavior.
Explain UDP delivery without automatic transport retransmission.
Trace TCP acknowledgements, timeouts, retransmission, buffering, and ordered application delivery.
Choose a protocol from an application's delivery requirements.

mission.title: Predict a transport outcome
mission.description: Choose a protocol, predict its behavior, then replay the simulator events.

introduction.title: Transport changes what happens after the network acts
introduction.content: Both TCP and UDP send data through a network that may delay, reorder, or lose packets. Their difference is how the transport layer responds.
points: UDP passes along surviving datagrams without automatically repairing a missing one.
This TCP-like model uses sequence numbers, ACKs, timeouts, retransmission, and in-order application delivery.

worked_example.title: One loss, two different consequences
worked_example.content: Imagine packets P1, P2, and P3 are sent, and the simulated network loses P2's first transmission.

steps.explanation: Surviving datagrams can reach the application; UDP does not automatically resend P2.
TCP notices the missing ACK, retransmits P2, and holds later data until order can be restored.
After repair, the TCP application receives the complete sequence in order.

worked_example.conclusion: The network caused the loss. The chosen transport protocol determined the response.

next.title: Now predict before replaying.
next.content: Use the displayed first-transmission conditions to reason about the receiver and application.

quiz.question: In this TCP-like model, packet P3 arrives while P2 is missing. What happens before the application receives P3?
options: P3 is delivered immediately out of order
P3 waits in the receiver buffer until P2 is repaired
The network changes P3 into an ACK

discovery.title: Transport behavior discovery
discovery.summary: The network may lose or reorder transmissions. UDP passes surviving datagrams onward without automatic repair, while this TCP-like model uses ACKs, timeout, retransmission, and buffering to deliver application data in order.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: TCP and UDP are transport protocols. The network conditions are separate from the protocol's response.

sections.title: UDP example
sections.content: If P2 is lost, P1 and P3 may still reach the application. UDP does not automatically resend P2 in this model.

sections.title: TCP example
sections.content: A missing ACK leads to timeout and retransmission. Later data can wait in a receiver buffer until order is restored.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Do not reduce the choice to fast versus slow. Ask whether the application requires repair and ordered delivery.

alternate_explanations.title: Postcards and numbered pages
alternate_explanations.content: UDP is like accepting whichever postcards arrive. TCP is like numbered pages: missing pages are requested again, and later pages wait before the book is read.

alternate_explanations.title: Follow one lost packet
alternate_explanations.content: P2 is lost. UDP leaves the gap. TCP waits for an ACK, times out, resends P2, then releases buffered P3 after P2.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how can the same packet loss produce different application results with UDP and TCP?
recall.model_answer: UDP does not automatically repair the missing datagram, while TCP uses acknowledgement, timeout, retransmission, and ordered delivery to repair the gap.
